subject: SPDE Model: Run times for varying n

messages.author: f50c1abb1614ea3a
messages.subject: SPDE Model: Run times for varying n
parts:
First off, I want to say thanks for all the work that the INLA put in their contribution to Spatial and Spatial-Temporal Bayesian models with R-INLA. Outstanding book and I am learning a lot.

I want to ask a general question about run-times. I know that run-times with the SPDE model are primarily functions of the number of vertices in the mesh. What about the number of points in the analysis? Should a SPDE model with 100 vertices but over 200,000 points run pretty fast? It seems as though that hasn't been the case for me, but I do not know if it is due to other factors.

Thanks,
Mike Gahan

On 16 Jul 2015, at 16:48, Mike Gahan <michae...@gmail.com> wrote:

First off, I want to say thanks for all the work that the INLA put in their contribution to Spatial and Spatial-Temporal Bayesian models with R-INLA. Outstanding book and I am learning a lot.

I want to ask a general question about run-times. I know that run-times with the SPDE model are primarily functions of the number of vertices in the mesh. What about the number of points in the analysis? Should a SPDE model with 100 vertices but over 200,000 points run pretty fast? It seems as though that hasn't been the case for me, but I do not know if it is due to other factors.

The runtime depends on the type of model. The fastest runtime should be for Gaussian data. It will take longer for nongaussian data, and models with more model parameters ("hyperparametrs" in inla terminology).
200,000 data points and 100 vertices should be faster than a model with 200,000 vertices, for example, but it's hard to say how much faster in general.

Finn


Thanks,
Mike Gahan
